readme: Shared HMAC test vectors for Tmesis stream keys (final plan 6.4, docs/TESTING.md 1.4).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Two implementations must agree byte for byte: tsp-web MINTS
stream keys and Tmesis only VERIFIES them. A disagreement about the signed string,
the encoding, or the hex case rejects every publish on the platform. Both sides
assert against THIS file: internal/keys/vectors_test.go reads it in Go, and a key
minter in any other language reads the same rows.
THE RULE THAT MAKES IT WORK. The fixture is generated from the Go implementation
(go test ./internal/keys -update) and a client NEVER edits it. A client that cannot
reproduce a row has a bug, and that is the finding, not a reason to adjust the
expected value. A shared fixture either side may rewrite is not a contract, it is a
diary.
HOW TO USE IT. For every entry in cases[]: decode secret_hex to bytes, build the
signed string as stream + "." + epoch, compute HMAC-SHA256 over it, hex encode
lowercase, and assert the result equals mac and that stream + "." + epoch + "." +
mac equals key. For every entry in negative[]: assert your parser or verifier
rejects key with the stated error class (malformed is decided from the shape alone;
bad_signature rows parse cleanly and fail the signature check against secret_hex).
ENCODING NOTES. secret_hex is authoritative and is the only form that can carry a
secret which is not valid UTF-8; secret_utf8 appears only when the bytes happen to
be valid UTF-8 and is informational. epoch is a JSON number and epoch_string is the
same value as a decimal string: read epoch_string in any language whose JSON parser
cannot hold an exact int64.
None of the secrets in this file are real. Do not use one for anything.

format.signed_string: stream + "." + epoch, with nothing else: no trailing newline, no length prefix, no separator after the epoch
format.mac: hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, signed_string)), lowercase, the full 64 characters
format.split: on the last two dots. The stream id charset forbids a dot, so a key with more than three fields is malformed rather than reinterpreted
format.stream_id: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,127}$ (docs/API.md section 8.1). It becomes the delivery prefix, so it is validated as a path component
format.epoch: the KEY epoch: base 10, unsigned, no leading zeros, no sign, and it must fit an int64

cases.name: stream id starting with a digit
stream id with underscores and digits
stream id at the 128 character cap
secret with bytes that are not valid UTF-8
unicode secret with a codepoint above the BMP
secret longer than the HMAC block size

negative.name: empty string
negative.reason: an empty key is not three fields

negative.name: no dots at all
negative.reason: one field, want three

negative.name: only one dot
negative.reason: two fields, want three

negative.name: a dot in the stream id, which would be four fields
negative.reason: the stream id charset forbids a dot, which is what keeps the split unambiguous

negative.name: trailing dot leaves an empty mac
negative.reason: the last field must be the mac

negative.name: empty stream id
negative.reason: the stream id is empty

negative.name: consecutive dots
negative.reason: an empty field is never valid

negative.name: uppercase stream id
negative.reason: the stream id is lowercase only: object stores disagree about whether Show-1 and show-1 are one prefix or two

negative.name: stream id with a leading dash
negative.reason: a value that reaches a command line must not look like a flag

negative.name: stream id with a forward slash
negative.reason: the stream id is a single path component and must not be able to add another

negative.name: stream id with parent directory traversal
negative.reason: the stream id becomes an output prefix

negative.name: stream id with a space
negative.reason: outside the charset

negative.name: stream id with a NUL byte
negative.reason: control characters reach logs, manifests, and object keys

negative.name: stream id with non-ASCII bytes
negative.reason: outside the charset

negative.name: stream id one byte over the 128 character cap
negative.reason: the cap is 128 characters

negative.name: empty epoch
negative.reason: the epoch is empty

negative.name: non-numeric epoch
negative.reason: the epoch is base 10 digits only

negative.name: negative epoch
negative.reason: the epoch is unsigned

negative.name: explicitly signed epoch
negative.reason: the epoch carries no sign, not even a plus

negative.name: epoch with a leading zero
negative.reason: one epoch value must have exactly one spelling, or the mac covers a string the verifier cannot reproduce

negative.name: epoch one above the int64 ceiling
negative.reason: the epoch must fit an int64

negative.name: epoch of twenty digits
negative.reason: the epoch must fit an int64

negative.name: mac truncated by one character
negative.reason: the mac is exactly 64 characters: a truncated mac is a weaker mac

negative.name: mac one character too long
negative.reason: the mac is exactly 64 characters

negative.name: uppercase hex mac
negative.reason: hex is lowercase: case folding would give one mac two valid spellings

negative.name: non-hex mac
negative.reason: the mac is hex

negative.name: mac minted with a different secret
negative.reason: correct length lowercase hex, wrong bytes: this is the row that exercises the constant time compare

negative.name: mac lifted from another epoch of the same stream
negative.reason: the epoch is part of the signed string, so an old mac does not survive a key epoch rotation

negative.name: mac lifted from another stream
negative.reason: the stream id is part of the signed string
